problem: Existing VLN benchmarks use small, fixed datasets on discrete/teleporting or weakly physical simulators (MP3D graphs, Habitat), reuse the same scans, and are fragmented across task types, which limits sim-to-real insight and LLM-scale training.
motivation: General-purpose embodied navigation agents need physics-aware, full-kinematics simulation, diverse new scenes, and a single framework spanning task types. Prior benchmarks (including VLN-PE on Isaac) add almost no new scenes and cover only fine-grained navigation. Agents built for collision-free graphs are expected to fail under real collisions.
key_idea: Build a large Isaac Sim-based VLN benchmark with 263 hand-crafted interactive USD scenes, five unified task types, and a scalable generation pipeline, and evaluate classic, foundation and MLLM agents with a physics-aware collision metric and a unified MoE baseline (GAMA).
insight: Under the Strict physics setting, zero-shot MLLM agents drop sharply: map-history SR goes from 25.53 (Tel-Hop) to 16.67 (Strict). CoT raises Tel-Hop SR (25.53 to 42.19) but not Strict SR (16.67 for the same map-history agent), so collision handling is the bottleneck rather than reasoning. Online fine-tuning of VLN-BERT lifts SR from 3.4 to 25.7, showing the domain gap is real and closable with interaction.
method: Simulator layer: Isaac Sim-based API with parameterizable physical agent embodiment (cylinder footprint, kinematics), physics-aware controller, and modular sensor rig (RGB, depth, LiDAR).
Environment layer: 263 hand-crafted interactive USD scenes with physical properties, 2D occupancy maps and a spatial-semantic scene graph used as ground-truth prior.
Path sampling: A* on an occupancy map dilated by the agent's height and diameter to obtain collision-free trajectories.

Instruction generation: scene-graph prior initialization, then a Describer (MLLM on frames), Verifier (cross-checks against the prior) and Synthesizer (formal/natural/casual styles), followed by human verification.
Task taxonomy: fine-grained, coarse-grained, visual-reference, long-horizon (2-3 chained sub-tasks) and dialogue with an LLM oracle; metrics add SR_n and Collision Rate.

Evaluation settings: offline training on pre-rendered data, online fine-tuning, and zero-shot MLLM agents in Strict (episode fails on 0.1 m displacement collision) vs Tel-Hop (teleport between waypoints) modes.

GAMA: HNR-style neural-radiance lookahead backbone with a State-Adaptive MoE policy (time-wise top-2 routing) and a unified action decoder treating discrete actions as Dirac priors with a residual for continuous control.

setting.backbone: GAMA (HNR + SAME MoE, trained); baselines CMA, Seq2Seq, RDP, HNR, VLN-BERT (trained); Qwen3-VL-4B (frozen) for text/map-history agents; InternNav-N1, NFM, Uni-NaVid (zero-shot)
setting.model_size: Qwen3-VL-4B for zero-shot agents; GAMA size not stated
setting.training_data: VLNVerse train split (offline, pre-rendered front-view RGB-D); online fine-tuning of VLN-BERT on the first 30 scenes, initialized from PREVALENT and VLN-CE-pretrained weights
setting.observation: egocentric front-view RGB 224x224 and depth 256x256 (90° FoV) offline; 12-view 360° panoramic rig online
setting.action_space: hybrid: low-level discrete actions and continuous control (4 primitives incl. stop); waypoints for online VLN-BERT
setting.privileged: none (occupancy map/scene graph are used only for data generation; the dialogue oracle is an LLM)

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 randomly sampled test trajectories across all test scenes (Strict/Tel-Hop table); the reported numbers appear to be computed over a small subset

numbers_note: Own GAMA results only on fine/coarse tasks; MLLM zero-shot results are on a 200-trajectory subset. Online VLN-BERT (Fine-tuned 10 epochs, 30 scenes): SR 25.7, SPL 23.7, NE 5.23, CR 19.5. Foundation-model baselines (NFM SR 51.59 on fine-grained test) are baselines and not listed.
results: GAMA achieves the best trained-model test SR/SPL of 37.72/33.85 (fine-grained) and 37.2/31.02 (coarse), beating RDP (36.38/32.29) on fine-grained. Zero-shot foundation models such as NFM reach higher SR (51.59) in some cases but with lower SPL. MLLM agents lose much of their performance under Strict physics (map-history SR 25.53 to 16.67), and dialogue raises SR to 67-85%.
limitations: Zero-shot MLLM evaluation uses only a 200-trajectory subset with a small 4B backbone; the Tel-Hop vs Strict comparison is on a small sample
GAMA gains over baselines are modest, with no ablation of SAME or the HNR backbone, and no real-robot experiments despite the sim-to-real motivation
Online fine-tuning is tested on only 30 scenes and a single model (VLN-BERT); instructions are LLM-generated with the oracle also an LLM
